I farm 349.9 mu here in Quzhou. That is a lot of land for one family, but I have been working it for 20 years and I know what the soil wants. I never went to school, but I learned by watching my father and my neighbors.

This year I will plant mostly sweetpotato because that is what does best on my land and I have buyers who come to collect it. I will keep some land for summer maize because we need grain for the house and to sell, and a smaller piece for millet on the poorer corner where sweetpotato doesn't do well.

For sweetpotato, I put about 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that is maybe 50 kg. The old men always told me sweetpotato loves potash, so I add one extra bag of potassium chloride for every 3-4 mu. If I skimp on potash the roots stay small and long instead of round and fat. I don't put too much nitrogen, because then the vines grow huge and the tubers stay tiny — I made that mistake one year when I was young and I won't do it again. I plough deep with a tractor, not just rotary, because sweetpotato needs loose soil to swell. I water twice from the well — once after planting and once when the roots are forming. I spray maybe twice, once for sweetpotato weevil and once if I see leaves eaten.

For summer maize, I follow what everyone around me does — about 2 bags of compound at planting and then top-dress with urea when it is knee-high, maybe half a bag per mu. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen per mu in total. I rotary till, plant the hybrid seed the dealer sells (everyone plants Zhengdan or the newer ones, I just buy what my neighbor buys), water twice from the well, spray once or twice for corn borer. I get around 550 kg per mu most years.

For millet, I don't spend much. Millet is tough, it grows with little. One bag of compound per mu, one watering if the rain is bad, one spray if worms come. I use the traditional seed I save from last year — millet doesn't need fancy seed. I get about 300 kg per mu.

I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than lose the crop. Fertilizer money I can earn back; a bad harvest I cannot.
